title: KkConditionScope throws away the State of its whole subtree whenever its condition (or the ambient one) flips
explanation: KkConditionScope.build returns `child` itself when the ambient condition already equals `condition`, and `KeikaiTheme(data: ..., child: child)` otherwise (lines 136-138). The two results put a different widget type in the same slot, so on every standby<->alert switch of a region Flutter cannot update the element: it unmounts the old subtree and inflates a new one. Every State below the scope is disposed and recreated. That is the normal use of this widget ("alert turns just this subtree red"; the web system's `Keikai.setCondition('alert', el)` only swaps custom properties and keeps the DOM). The same happens to a region pinned to one condition when the app condition flips around it. Visible effects: scroll offsets jump to 0, text input, focus and counters are lost, tickers restart, and every one-shot entrance (KkOneShot / KkBoot wipe) of the region plays again at the moment of the alarm. Note that test/foundation/theme_test.dart:190 ('a scope with the condition already in force adds nothing') pins this shape toggle (findsOneWidget, then findsNWidgets(2)) and has to change with the fix.
evidence:
Throwaway tests, run with `flutter test test/_review/tokens-theme/condition_scope_test.dart` (directory deleted afterwards).

class _Probe extends StatefulWidget {...}  // State: int taps; build: GestureDetector(onTap: () => setState(() => taps++), child: SizedBox(width: 100, height: 40, child: Text('taps $taps')))
Widget tree(KkCondition c) => Directionality(textDirection: TextDirection.ltr, child: KeikaiTheme(data: const KeikaiThemeData(),
    child: Align(alignment: Alignment.topLeft, child: KkConditionScope(condition: c, child: const _Probe()))));
await tester.pumpWidget(tree(KkCondition.standby)); await tester.tap(find.byType(_Probe)); await tester.pump();   // 'taps 1'
final before = tester.state(find.byType(_Probe));
await tester.pumpWidget(tree(KkCondition.alert));
expect(identical(before, tester.state(find.byType(_Probe))), isTrue);

Output:
A1 standby->alert: same State=false old mounted=false text="taps 0"
  Expected: true
    Actual: <false>
  the State under the scope was thrown away by a condition switch
A2 (const KkConditionScope(condition: KkCondition.standby, child: _Probe()) under pumpKk, then pumpKk(..., condition: KkCondition.alert)):
  A2 app standby->alert: same State=false old mounted=false text="taps 0"
A3 (ListView in the scope, position.jumpTo(400), then the scope goes standby->alert):
  A3 scroll offset after standby->alert: 0.0 (was 400.0)
  Expected: <400>
    Actual: <0.0>
A4 (KkOneShot(duration: KkMotion.boot) in the scope, motion: true, 2 s pumped so it has finished, then standby->alert):
  A4 entrance progress before the switch: 1.0
  A4 entrance progress right after standby->alert: 0.0, 210ms later: 0.5
  Expected: <1.0>
    Actual: <0.0>
  the boot entrance of the region started again
suggestedFix: Return the same widget shape for both cases, e.g. always `return KeikaiTheme(data: data.withCondition(condition), child: child);` (withCondition already returns the same object when nothing changes, and _KeikaiThemeScope.updateShouldNotify compares by value, so there is no extra rebuild). Better, combine it with the next finding: always build `_KeikaiThemeScope(data: next, child: DefaultTextStyle(<ambient style, re-inked>, child: child))`. Update the 'adds nothing' test to assert State preservation instead of the widget count.

title: KkConditionScope replaces the ambient DefaultTextStyle (size, family, alignment, maxLines, overflow) instead of only switching the condition, and only when the condition differs
explanation: When the scope's condition differs from the ambient one it inserts a full KeikaiTheme, whose build (lines 110-113) installs a brand new `DefaultTextStyle(style: bodyMd in ink)` with default textAlign / softWrap / overflow / maxLines. Any DefaultTextStyle set between the outer theme and the scope is discarded: the region falls back to body 14/1.55 IBM Plex Sans KR, left aligned, unlimited lines, clip. When the condition equals the ambient one the scope is a pass-through and the ambient style survives. So the typography and the layout of a region change at the moment it turns to alert (and change back when it returns), although the widget is documented as switching "only the condition" (KeikaiTheme doc) / turning the subtree red. KkText and KkIcon take their colour from the ambient DefaultTextStyle, so an ancestor colour such as ink-dim is replaced by ink in the same way. In the web system a `data-theme` attribute only redefines colour variables; inherited font size, family and alignment are untouched.
evidence:
Throwaway test (same deleted file):

KeikaiTheme(data: const KeikaiThemeData(), child: Align(alignment: Alignment.topLeft, child: SizedBox(width: 300,
  child: DefaultTextStyle.merge(
    style: const TextStyle(fontSize: 30, fontFamily: 'packages/keikai/IBM Plex Mono'),
    textAlign: TextAlign.center, maxLines: 1, overflow: TextOverflow.ellipsis,
    child: KkConditionScope(condition: c, child: Builder(builder: (context) { seen = DefaultTextStyle.of(context); return const Text('ALARM'); }))))))

Output (c = standby, then c = alert):
B same condition : size=30.0 family=packages/keikai/IBM Plex Mono align=TextAlign.center maxLines=1 overflow=TextOverflow.ellipsis textHeight=47.0
B other condition: size=14.0 family=packages/keikai/IBM Plex Sans KR align=null maxLines=null overflow=TextOverflow.clip textHeight=22.0
  Expected: <30>
    Actual: <14.0>
  font size of the region changed with the condition
suggestedFix: In KkConditionScope do not go through KeikaiTheme. Read `DefaultTextStyle.of(context)` and re-emit it under the new `_KeikaiThemeScope` with the same textAlign, softWrap, overflow, maxLines, textWidthBasis and textHeightBehavior, changing only the colour: if the ambient colour is the outgoing theme's ink, replace it with the new theme's ink (when there is no DefaultTextStyle above, keep the current bodyMd-in-ink default). Emit this wrapper for both the equal and the different condition so the tree shape stays fixed (see the previous finding).

title: KeikaiTheme.motionOf ignores the platform's Reduce Motion request (iOS): strobes, blinks and wipes keep running
explanation: motionOf is documented as "the theme allows motion and the platform has not asked for reduced motion", and the design system requires that with prefers-reduced-motion everything is switched off ("와이프·스크램블·흐름·점멸 없이 최종 상태만 보이고, 스트로브는 고정 채움이 된다"). The implementation only reads MediaQuery.disableAnimations. In the Flutter SDK used here that flag is Android's "Remove animations"; the iOS "Reduce Motion" setting is reported through the separate AccessibilityFeatures.reduceMotion / MediaQueryData.reduceMotion flag and does not set disableAnimations. Every motion widget of the package gates on motionOf (KkPhaseBuilder, KkBlink, KkLoop, KkOneShot, KkScramble, KkGlitch, page routes), so on an iPhone with Reduce Motion on, the 1.2 s alarm strobe, the blinks, hazards and wipes all still play, while the web original on the same device is static. The existing test (test/foundation/theme_test.dart:121) only covers disableAnimations.

title: KkMetrics.rowsHeight(0) returns -8 (a negative height) instead of 0
explanation: `rowsHeight(int rows) => rows * rowUnit + (rows - 1) * gridGutter` subtracts one gutter even when there are no rows, so zero rows give -gridGutter (-8) and negative counts go further down. The method is public API documented as "Height of a grid cell that spans [rows] row units" and its natural input is a row count such as RenderKkGrid.resolvedRows, which is 0 for an empty grid. Feeding the result to a box asserts in debug builds. The grid's own copy of the same formula guards the case (lib/src/layout/grid.dart:286: `rows <= 0 ? 0 : rows * _rowUnit + (rows - 1) * _gutter`), so the two disagree at 0.
suggestedFix: double rowsHeight(int rows) => rows <= 0 ? 0 : rows * rowUnit + (rows - 1) * gridGutter;  (and let RenderKkGrid._heightFor call it so there is one formula).

title: kkMix is not CSS color-mix(in srgb) for translucent operands (straight lerp instead of premultiplied)
explanation: kkMix is exported and documented as "`color-mix(in srgb, a amount, b)`". It is implemented as `Color.lerp(b, a, amount)`, which interpolates the four channels independently (unpremultiplied). CSS color-mix interpolates premultiplied colours, so the two agree only when both operands are opaque. With a translucent operand the hue is wrong: mixing with transparent darkens the colour toward black instead of keeping it, and the CSS Color 5 worked example comes out with red and green swapped in weight. Every call inside the package today passes opaque tokens (KkColors.ramp, charts/status_timeline.dart:337, charts/bar_list.dart:210), where the result is exact, so this only bites callers who pass a translucent colour (a custom theme colour or a series colour with alpha).
evidence:
Throwaway test (values_test.dart, deleted afterwards):

kkMix(const Color(0xFFFF7A1A), 0.55, const Color(0x00000000));
kkMix(const Color.from(alpha: 0.7, red: 1, green: 0, blue: 0), 0.25, const Color.from(alpha: 0.2, red: 0, green: 1, blue: 0));

Output:
M1 kkMix(#ff7a1a, .55, transparent) = r=0.55000 g=0.26314 b=0.05608 a=0.550
M1 kkFade(#ff7a1a, .55)             = r=1.00000 g=0.47843 b=0.10196 a=0.550   <- what CSS color-mix gives
M1 kkMix(red/.7, .25, green/.2)     = r=0.25000 g=0.75000 b=0.00000 a=0.325   CSS: r=0.53846 g=0.46154 b=0 a=0.325
  Expected: a numeric value within <0.0001> of <0.53846>
    Actual: <0.25>
(The second input is the example of CSS Color 5: color-mix(in srgb, rgb(100% 0% 0% / 0.7) 25%, rgb(0% 100% 0% / 0.2)) = color(srgb 0.53846 0.46154 0 / 0.325); premultiplied: r = .7*.25/.325, g = .2*.75/.325.)
Opaque control passes: kkMix(#ff7a1a, 0.08, #050506) = rgb(25.0, 14.36, 7.6).

title: glowTrace halves the halo of the glow-trace token: a drop-shadow length is the Gaussian sigma, not a box-shadow blur radius
explanation: KkGlow.blur is defined as a box-shadow style value ("CSS blur radius of the halo (the Gaussian sigma is half of it)", line 23) and every painter converts it with `blur / 2`. That is right for glow-signal and glow-alert, which are box-shadows. glow-trace is different: the token is `0 0 4px #5cff9d99` with the usage "filter: drop-shadow() 안에 넣어", and bundle.css:508 applies it as `filter: drop-shadow(var(--glow-trace))`. In CSS Filter Effects the third length of drop-shadow() is the standard deviation itself (the spec says the values are interpreted as for box-shadow "but with the optional 3rd <length> value being the standard deviation instead of blur radius"; the markup equivalent is feGaussianBlur stdDeviation="[radius]"). So the web halo has sigma 4, while `KkGlow(ring: 0, blur: 4)` means sigma 2 under the class's own convention: the phosphor bloom of a live trace is half as wide as designed. The colour and alpha (#5cff9d at 0x99) are correct.
evidence:
Not executed in a browser (none available; the spec host www.w3.org is outside this session's allowed network domains and would have to be allowed in the session's network settings to re-fetch the text, so the quotation is from the Filter Effects Level 1 definition of drop-shadow() as I know it).
Exact lines:
tokens.json: "name": "glow-trace", "value": { "standby": "0 0 4px #5cff9d99", "alert": "0 0 4px #5cff9d99" }, "usage": "filter: drop-shadow() 안에 넣어 파형 선의 형광 번짐."
bundle.css:508:   filter: drop-shadow(var(--glow-trace));
colors.dart:23:   /// CSS blur radius of the halo (the Gaussian sigma is half of it).
colors.dart:198:  KkGlow get glowTrace => KkGlow(color: nominal, ring: 0, blur: 4, alpha: 0.6);
consumer, lib/src/charts/trace.dart:226:  ..maskFilter = MaskFilter.blur(BlurStyle.normal, g.blur / 2),
A throwaway test printed: "G glowTrace: ring=0.0 blur=4.0 -> sigma by the KkGlow convention = 2.0" (CSS: sigma 4.0). The same halving applies to the per-level variant in trace.dart:97, `KkGlow(color: ink, ring: 0, blur: 3, alpha: 1)` for `drop-shadow(0 0 3px currentColor)` (bundle.css:510).
suggestedFix: Keep KkGlow's convention and store the equivalent blur radius: `KkGlow get glowTrace => KkGlow(color: nominal, ring: 0, blur: 8, alpha: 0.6);` (sigma 4), with a comment that drop-shadow tokens carry a sigma; use blur: 6 for the 3px per-level variant in charts/trace.dart. Update the pinned value in test/foundation/tokens_test.dart:263.

title: Time scale is applied twice to KkLoop-driven effects: hazard and marquee run at 1/timeScale² speed
explanation: KkLoop (lib/src/motion/loops.dart:132-135, a reviewed file) already divides the shared clock by motion.timeScale before handing it to its builder; the class doc does not say so. KkHazard (effects.dart:55) and KkMarquee (effects.dart:136) then also stretch their period with theme.motion.scaled(...) and evaluate kkLoopAt(time.value, period), so the scale is applied twice. With timeScale 2 ("half speed") the hazard takes 3.6s per stripe period instead of 1.8s, and the marquee four times its period instead of two. The same pattern is in the unfinished charts (cited, not run): charts/trace.dart:110 and charts/radar.dart:198-199. The radar's critical blink then has a period of 1.2s x scale² and no longer flips together with KkBlink/KkStrobe (1.2s x scale), which breaks the "all loops stay in step" promise of kkFrameTime. Other consumers (_CrtPainter at effects.dart:277/290, controls/empty.dart:146, diagram/painter.dart:423) use the scaled clock with unscaled periods, which is the correct single scaling, so the package is inconsistent with itself. effects.dart is outside the five assigned files; reported because the defect comes from the contract of KkLoop.
evidence: Throwaway test: RepaintBoundary(KkHazard(width: 200, height: 24, running: true)) under KeikaiThemeData(motion: KkMotion(timeScale: 2)); boundary.toImage() bytes compared at t, t+1.8s, t+3.6s. Output: "same after 1.8s: false; same after 3.6s: true" then "Expected: true  Actual: <false>  0.9s x timeScale 2 = 1.8s per stripe period". Control at timeScale 1 passes (image repeats after 0.9s, differs after 0.45s). KkMarquee('CRITICAL 0123', period: 1s): "scale=1.0 same after half=false one=true two periods=true" but "scale=2.0 same after half=false one=false two periods=true" (repeats after 4s, not 2s).
suggestedFix: Keep KkLoop as the single place where timeScale is applied and pass unscaled periods to the painters: period: KkMotion.hazard at effects.dart:55, period: period at effects.dart:136, and the same at charts/trace.dart:110 and charts/radar.dart:198-199. Add one sentence to the KkLoop doc that the clock is already time-scaled.

title: iOS "Reduce Motion" does not switch motion off: motionOf only reads disableAnimations
explanation: Every widget in the reviewed motion files decides whether to animate through KeikaiTheme.motionOf, and the KkMotion doc (lib/src/foundation/motion.dart:88-90) promises that "when the platform asks for reduced motion, every animation is skipped". The design README requires everything off under prefers-reduced-motion. motionOf checks only MediaQuery.maybeDisableAnimationsOf, which is Android's "Remove animations". The framework doc of MediaQueryData.disableAnimations in the installed SDK states: "On iOS, reduced motion is exposed separately via AccessibilityFeatures.reduceMotion and does not set this flag". So an iOS user with Reduce Motion on (the setting Safari maps to prefers-reduced-motion) still gets wipes, scrambles, strobes, blinks and the full-screen glitch with three red flashes. theme.dart is outside the five assigned files; reported because it is the gate all of them use.
evidence: Throwaway test: tester.platformDispatcher.accessibilityFeaturesTestValue = const FakeAccessibilityFeatures(reduceMotion: true); pump KkBlink with motion on and sample Opacity for 1.3s. Output: "MediaQuery.reduceMotion=true KeikaiTheme.motionOf=true blink opacities seen={1.0, 0.2}" then "Expected: false  Actual: <true>  the platform asked for reduced motion". The control with FakeAccessibilityFeatures(disableAnimations: true) passes (motionOf false, opacity stays 1.0).
suggestedFix: In motionOf also return false when MediaQuery.maybeReduceMotionOf(context) is true (it exists in the pinned Flutter 3.50.1; check it against the pubspec lower bound flutter >=3.35.0 and raise the bound if needed). Add a test next to the existing disableAnimations one.

title: Every KkScramble of the same text length shows the same noise digits at the same time
explanation: The noise is _hash(seed, step, i) with seed = _generation * 31 + widget.text.length (line 153); nothing depends on the value or on the widget instance. The language fixes digit counts (042.7, 078), so the readouts on a screen normally have equal length, and they mount in the same frame with _generation == 1. They therefore all display literally the same number for the first steps and share the same unsettled tail until the end: a row of stats flashes "965.1" in unison instead of each value churning by itself (README: digits scramble per position, then settle from the front). Cosmetic, but it happens in normal use on every screen with two or more numeric readouts.
evidence:
Throwaway test: four KkScramble widgets ('042.7', '078.3', '113.9', '256.0') in a Column, motion on, shown text sampled every 46ms:
t=  0ms  965.1  965.1  965.1  965.1
t= 46ms  965.1  965.1  965.1  965.1
t= 92ms  006.6  006.6  006.6  006.6
t=138ms  017.1  017.1  117.1  217.1
t=230ms  041.2  071.2  111.2  251.2
t=414ms  042.5  078.5  113.5  256.5
"Expected: <0>  Actual: <3>  frames in which all four readouts showed exactly the same digits".
suggestedFix: Fold the target into the seed, for example by running the code units of widget.text through _hash, so different values churn differently while the output stays deterministic for goldens. KkStagger.of(context) can be added as a further salt for equal values.

title: KkPhaseBuilder keeps the old phase when phases, period or time scale change; builder can receive phase >= phases
explanation: _sync() returns early when the running state is unchanged (line 49). After didUpdateWidget or didChangeDependencies with a different phases, period or motion.timeScale, build() (line 79) passes the _phase that the last tick computed for the old parameters; it is corrected only by the next tick, one frame later. Reducing phases hands the builder an index outside the documented 0 to phases-1 range, so a builder that indexes a list throws for that frame. Changing only the period paints one frame in the wrong phase; hud/annunciator.dart:322 does this when a tile goes from alarm (500ms) to return-to-normal (1.2s).
evidence: Throwaway test 1: run KkPhaseBuilder(period: 400ms, phases: 4) until it reports phase 3, then rebuild with phases: 2. Output: "Expected: empty  Actual: ['3/2']  builder calls (phase/phases): [0/4, 1/4, 2/4, 3/4, 3/2, 1/2]". Throwaway test 2: rebuild from period 500ms to 1200ms at a moment where the two loops are in different phases; the builder logged "period=1200 phase=1 clock=0" and one frame later "period=1200 phase=0 clock=0" (clock = kkPhaseAt(kkFrameTime(), 1200ms)).
suggestedFix: In _sync(), whenever shouldRun is true, recompute _phase = kkPhaseAt(kkFrameTime(), _period, phases: widget.phases) before the early return, so every build uses the current parameters.

title: KkLoop paints its first frame at time zero instead of the shared clock
explanation: When the loop starts, _sync() only starts the ticker (line 143). _time stays Duration.zero until the first tick, which arrives in the next frame. The frame in which a KkLoop is mounted or re-enabled is therefore painted at loop position 0, and the next frame jumps to the position of the shared clock: a one-frame jump of hazard stripes, radar sweep or waveform, during which the loop is not in step with the other loops. KkPhaseBuilder initialises its phase from the clock at the same point (line 52); KkLoop does not.
evidence: Throwaway test: let the frame clock run for 1234ms, then pumpWidget a KkLoop whose CustomPainter(repaint: time) records time.value on paint. Output: "Expected: Duration:<0:00:01.234000>  Actual: Duration:<0:00:00.000000>  first painted time 0:00:00.000000, shared clock 0:00:01.234000".
suggestedFix: When starting in _sync(), set _time.value from kkFrameTime() divided by _scale before calling start(); move the scaling into a helper shared with _tick.

title: KkScramble with steps <= 0 never settles: the readout stays on random digits
explanation: _onTick rebuilds only when floor(value * steps) changes (lines 109-110). With steps: 0 it is always 0, and with a negative count it already equals steps just before the end, so the last tick (value 1) never calls setState. The widget keeps showing the noise of an earlier frame until something else rebuilds it, which is a wrong number on screen. Unlike KkSteps there is no assert on the count (constructor line 75).
evidence: Throwaway test: KkScramble('31337', steps: n), motion on, pumped for 1.2s (duration is 0.46s), then the Text data read: "steps=0 shown after 1.2s: 96551", "steps=-1 shown after 1.2s: 55372", "steps=-3 shown after 1.2s: 31395", "steps=1 shown after 1.2s: 31337". Only steps=1 passes expect(shown, '31337').
suggestedFix: Add assert(steps > 0) to the constructor, and make the end independent of the step count: also call setState when the controller completes (status listener, or when _controller.value >= 1 and the shown text is not yet the target).

title: KkSteppedValue keeps animating after motion is switched off mid-transition
explanation: _KkSteppedValueState.didChangeDependencies (lines 331-337) only handles its first call. When KeikaiTheme.motionOf turns false while a transition is running (platform reduced motion, or KkMotion.enabled set to false), the controller is left running and the value keeps stepping to the end. KkOneShot in the same file jumps to the final state in this situation (lines 92-96), and in the CSS source the reduced-motion rule sets transition: none on the meter bars (bundle.css:2551), which cancels a running transition. README: with reduced motion only the final state is shown.
evidence: Throwaway test: KkSteppedValue 0 -> 100 with duration 1s and 10 steps, pump 250ms (shown is 20), set tester.platformDispatcher.accessibilityFeaturesTestValue = FakeAccessibilityFeatures(disableAnimations: true), pump twice. Output: "Expected: <100>  Actual: <20.0>". The equivalent existing test for KkOneShot ('turning reduced motion on mid-flight jumps to the end') passes.
suggestedFix: In didChangeDependencies add: else if (_controller.isAnimating && !KeikaiTheme.motionOf(context)) { _controller.value = 1; _shown = _to; }

title: KkScramble keeps churning after motion is switched off mid-scramble
explanation: Same gap as KkSteppedValue. didChangeDependencies (lines 124-130) ignores every call after the first, and didUpdateWidget (lines 133-136) only looks at text. A scramble in flight therefore continues to show wrong digits after reduced motion is turned on (or enabled becomes false) until its duration has passed, while KkOneShot jumps to the final state.
evidence: Throwaway test: KkScramble('0000000000', duration: 2s), motion on, pump 250ms, set FakeAccessibilityFeatures(disableAnimations: true), pump twice. Output: "Expected: '0000000000'  Actual: '0793653953'".
suggestedFix: In didChangeDependencies (after the first call) and in didUpdateWidget: if (_controller.isAnimating && (!widget.enabled || !KeikaiTheme.motionOf(context))) _controller.value = 1;

title: KkOneShot.onDone never fires when the animation is skipped or cut short
explanation: onDone is called only from the controller's completed status (line 56). The paths that finish the one-shot without running the controller to its end set _done = true but never call it: motion off or enabled: false (lines 63-68), zero total length (lines 74-78), and reduced motion turned on mid-flight (lines 92-96). The builder is told done, the callback is not. A caller that cleans up in onDone is never notified: hud/data_log.dart:225 and :347 remove a row from the _fresh set there, so with reduced motion on the rows stay marked as new, and the "new row" flash plays for old rows once motion is back and ListView.builder remounts them on scroll (this consequence is from reading the code, not run, because hud is not exported).
evidence: Throwaway tests: (a) motion off, KkOneShot(duration: 200ms, onDone: () => calls++), pump 500ms: "Expected: <1>  Actual: <0>". (b) motion on, 1s one-shot, FakeAccessibilityFeatures(disableAnimations: true) set at 100ms, pump 2s: printed "done=true onDone calls=0". (c) motion on, duration: Duration.zero: printed "done=true onDone calls=0".
suggestedFix: Whenever _done is set without the controller completing, schedule the callback once for that run, for example SchedulerBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback((_) { if (mounted) widget.onDone?.call(); }), so it is not invoked during build.

title: Scramble step still uses a raw floor: a frame on a step edge repeats the previous noise frame
explanation: lib/src/foundation/motion.dart on disk now routes KkSteps and kkKeyframes through kkStepDown, which absorbs rounding error at step edges (with it, my probe of 344 exact step edges through real AnimationControllers shows 0 wrong; before it 93 were one step behind). KkScramble was not updated: it computes the noise step with (_controller.value * widget.steps).floor() at lines 109 and 152, and kkScrambleText computes the settled count with a raw floor at line 19. On a frame that lands exactly on a step edge the product is for example 0.9999999999999999, so the previous noise frame is shown again and one digit fewer is settled (at 414ms of 460ms with 30 digits, 26 are settled instead of 27).
evidence:
Throwaway test: KkScramble('0' * 30), motion on, pumped exactly 46ms per frame (0.46s / 10 steps); last ten characters of the shown text:
t=0ms 8742506110
t=46ms 8742506110
t=92ms 5374431245
t=138ms 1475411586
t=184ms 1475411586
t=230ms 1388068896
t=276ms 6714292278
t=322ms 0941324916
t=368ms 0941324916
t=414ms 0000007384
"Expected: <10>  Actual: <7>  0.46s / 10 steps = one new noise frame every 46ms".
suggestedFix: Use the same tolerance as kkStepDown: (_controller.value * widget.steps + 1e-9).floor() in _onTick and in build, and (progress.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * scrambleable + 1e-9).floor() for settled in kkScrambleText.

title: KkMarquee in unbounded width takes an infinite size and its painter never returns (the app freezes)
explanation: KkMarquee always asks for an infinite width (line 131: `CustomPaint(size: Size(double.infinity, ...))`). Under an unbounded width constraint (a non-flex child of a Row / KkRow, a horizontal scroll view, UnconstrainedBox) RenderCustomPaint therefore gets Size(Infinity, 13). The painter then runs `for (double x = -shift; x < size.width; x += unit) tp.paint(...)` (line 178) with size.width == infinity, which never terminates and keeps recording paragraphs into the picture. In a debug build the layout assertion is only reported (not rethrown) and the same frame goes on to paint, so the app prints one error and then hangs; in a release build there is no assertion at all, just the hang and growing memory. Other width-filling widgets fail with an error here; this one freezes the isolate.
suggestedFix: Never hand the painter an infinite width. Build inside a LayoutBuilder (or a small render object) and use `constraints.hasBoundedWidth ? double.infinity : textWidth + gap` as the CustomPaint width, and guard the painter as well: `if (text.isEmpty || size.width <= 0 || !size.width.isFinite) return;`.

title: KkCrt changes the shape of its subtree with its flags, so switching scanlines / sweep / noise destroys and recreates the child's State
explanation: KkCrt.build returns three different trees: `child` itself when all effects are off (line 215), `CustomPaint(child)` for scan lines only (line 225), and `KkLoop(builder -> CustomPaint(child))` when sweep or noise is on (line 226). The child therefore sits at a different depth / under a different parent type depending on the flags, so every time a flag crosses one of those boundaries the framework unmounts the whole child subtree and builds a new one. Anything stateful inside is lost: scroll offsets, focus and text of inputs, running tickers, and in this design language every boot wipe / flicker / stagger of the panels inside replays. The natural uses are exactly such toggles: `KkCrt(noise: !hasSignal, scanlines: false, child: feed)` for a 'no signal' display, or `KkCrt(sweep: live, child: panel)`.
evidence:
Throwaway test with a StatefulWidget child that counts initState / dispose, re-pumped through the same harness (state is kept when the shape does not change):

  await pumpKk(tester, const KkCrt(scanlines: false, child: _Probe()));            // initState x1
  await pumpKk(tester, const KkCrt(scanlines: false, noise: true, child: _Probe()));
  await pumpKk(tester, const KkCrt(child: _Probe()));
  await pumpKk(tester, const KkCrt(sweep: true, child: _Probe()));

Output:
  all off -> noise on:        initState x2, dispose x1
  noise -> scan lines only:   initState x3, dispose x2
  scan lines -> + sweep:      initState x4, dispose x3
  Expected: [1, 1, 1, 0]
    Actual: [2, 3, 4, 3]
  the child State must survive

Control from an earlier run of the same test: going from `scanlines + noise` to `scanlines + noise + sweep` (same tree shape) left the counters unchanged (`+sweep (control, same shape): inits=3 disposes=2`, same as the line before it).
suggestedFix: Build one fixed chain whatever the flags are, for example `KkLoop(enabled: sweep || noise, builder: (context, time) => CustomPaint(foregroundPainter: (scanlines || sweep || noise) ? _CrtPainter(..., time: (sweep || noise) ? time : null) : null, child: child))`. A disabled KkLoop starts no ticker, so scan lines alone stay static. The existing test that expects no CustomPaint ancestor when everything is off has to be relaxed accordingly.

title: RenderKkGlitch clips its child to its own box for the whole 0.7s, although kk-glitch has clip-path: none outside the two slices
explanation: `Rect clip = Offset.zero & size;` (line 438) is the default and `pushClipRect` is called unconditionally while the animation is active (line 448), including the last 0.2s when only the flash timeline is still running. In the CSS the clip-path is `none` at 0%, 80% and 100% of kk-glitch; only the two inset() slices clip. So everything the child paints outside its box disappears for 0.7s and pops back: the KkGlow ring and halo (KkDecoration draws them outside the rect), the corner brackets ('slightly outside the box'), focus rings, overflowing content. The root KkGlitch of KeikaiApp is not visibly affected because nothing lies outside the window, but `.kk-glitch:not(html)` and the public KkGlitch widget are meant for single elements such as an alarm panel, which carries exactly such a glow.
evidence:
Throwaway test: a 40x40 KkBox with `KkDecoration(fill: black, glow: KkColors.standby.glowAlert)` inside `KkGlitch(flash: false)`, centred in a 100x100 black RepaintBoundary (box at (30,30)-(70,70)); pixel (29,50) is the 1px glow ring. Read back with RenderRepaintBoundary.toImage at rest, at 600 / 650 / 690ms after the trigger (the 0.5s glitch is over: transform none, clip-path none) and after the end:

  glow ring pixel (29,50): at rest #f8283c | during 600ms #000000, 650ms #000000, 690ms #000000 | after #f8283c
  Expected: true  Actual: <false>  (the glow ring stays visible)
suggestedFix: Keep the clip nullable and only push a clip layer during the slice phases: `if (clip == null) { _clipLayer.layer = null; super.paint(c, o); } else { _clipLayer.layer = c.pushClipRect(needsCompositing, o, clip, super.paint, oldLayer: _clipLayer.layer); }`.

title: The glitch skew pivots on the top-left corner instead of the centre of the box (CSS transform-origin is 50% 50%)
explanation: The matrix is `identity..setEntry(0, 1, tan(skew))..setEntry(0, 3, dx)` (lines 444-446) and PaintingContext.pushTransform applies it about the box origin, so x' = x + dx + tan(skew)·y with y measured from the top edge. bundle.css sets no transform-origin for `html.kk-glitch body` / `.kk-glitch`, so `translateX(-7px) skewX(-5deg)` shears about the centre: x' = x + dx + tan(skew)·(y − H/2). The code therefore adds an extra uniform shift of tan(5°)·H/2 to the left at the peak: the nominal 7px displacement becomes about 33px at the centre of an 800x600 window (about 54px on a 1080px-high screen), the top edge does not swing right at all, and the bottom edge swings twice as far left, opening a wedge of background on the right only. It happens on every glitch, for the 0.2s in which the skew is non-zero.
evidence:
Throwaway test: `KkGlitch(flash: false, child: SizedBox(width: 800, height: 600))`, trigger changed, pumped to 105ms (just past the 20% keyframe: translateX(-7px) skewX(-5deg)), then RenderKkGlitch.paint recorded with offset zero and the transform matrix applied to three points:

  painted: top-left (-7.0, 0)  centre (366.8, 300)  bottom-left (-59.5, 600)
  CSS:     top-left (19.2, 0)  centre (393.0, 300)  bottom-left (-33.2, 600)
  Expected: 393.0 (±0.01)
    Actual: <366.7534009422228>
  the centre only moves by translateX(-7px)

`grep transform-origin bundle.css` shows no rule for .kk-glitch or body, so the default 50% 50% applies.
suggestedFix: Shear about the centre: `..setEntry(0, 1, math.tan(skew))..setEntry(0, 3, dx - math.tan(skew) * size.height / 2)`.

title: The glitch slices appear in the wrong windows and jump instead of stepping: clip-path is not evaluated per keyframe interval with steps(5, end)
explanation: The code shows inset(12% 0 52% 0) for g in [0.3, 0.5) and inset(58% 0 9% 0) for g in [0.5, 0.7) (lines 439-443), i.e. it assumes a hard cut halfway between neighbouring keyframes. In kk-glitch the clip-path keyframes are 0% none, 40% inset(12% 0 52% 0), 60% inset(58% 0 9% 0), 80% none (the 20% keyframe does not set clip-path, so for this property it does not exist), and `steps(5, end)` applies to each of those intervals, exactly as the code already does for the transform. none <-> inset() is a discrete animation that flips when the stepped progress reaches 0.5, i.e. at 0.6 of the interval: the first slice starts at 24% (0.12s), not 30%, and the last one ends at 72% (0.36s), not 70%. inset() <-> inset() interpolates (the design relies on that for kk-boot, `inset(0 100% 0 0)` -> `inset(0 0 0 0)` in 7 steps), so between 40% and 60% the visible band slides down in five steps (top 12 / 21.2 / 30.4 / 39.6 / 48.8 %, bottom 52 / 43.4 / 34.8 / 26.2 / 17.6 %) instead of cutting from one band to the other at 50%.
evidence:
Throwaway test: `KkGlitch(flash: false, child: SizedBox(width: 200, height: 100))`, sampled every 10ms; the clip rect recorded from RenderKkGlitch.paint is compared with a model of the CSS (per-interval steps(5, end), discrete flip at 0.5, inset interpolation). Mismatches printed:

  125ms: painted none, CSS inset(12.0% 0 52.0% 0)
  135ms: painted none, CSS inset(12.0% 0 52.0% 0)
  145ms: painted none, CSS inset(12.0% 0 52.0% 0)
  225ms: painted inset(12.0% 0 52.0% 0), CSS inset(21.2% 0 43.4% 0)
  235ms: painted inset(12.0% 0 52.0% 0), CSS inset(21.2% 0 43.4% 0)
  245ms: painted inset(12.0% 0 52.0% 0), CSS inset(30.4% 0 34.8% 0)
  255ms: painted inset(58.0% 0 9.0% 0), CSS inset(30.4% 0 34.8% 0)
  265ms: painted inset(58.0% 0 9.0% 0), CSS inset(39.6% 0 26.2% 0)
  275ms: painted inset(58.0% 0 9.0% 0), CSS inset(39.6% 0 26.2% 0)
  285ms: painted inset(58.0% 0 9.0% 0), CSS inset(48.8% 0 17.6% 0)
  295ms: painted inset(58.0% 0 9.0% 0), CSS inset(48.8% 0 17.6% 0)
  355ms: painted none, CSS inset(58.0% 0 9.0% 0)

The CSS side is derived from the specification rules (missing property in a keyframe, timing function per keyframe interval, discrete flip at 50%), not from a browser run.
suggestedFix: Derive the clip the same way as the transform: `double st(double d) => (d * 5).floorToDouble() / 5;` then `if (g < 0.4) { if (st(g / 0.4) >= 0.5) clip = inset(12, 52); } else if (g < 0.6) { final k = st((g - 0.4) / 0.2); clip = inset(12 + 46 * k, 52 - 43 * k); } else if (g < 0.8) { if (st((g - 0.6) / 0.2) < 0.5) clip = inset(58, 9); }` (percentages of the height; no clip otherwise).

title: KkLoop starts at time zero, so the first painted frame of every running hazard, marquee and CRT overlay is out of step and then snaps
explanation: Found while checking the phase of the widgets in effects.dart; the cause is in KkLoop, which they all use. `_KkLoopState._time` is created as Duration.zero and `_sync()` only starts the ticker (line 143); the notifier gets its first real value in `_tick`, i.e. on the frame after the one that mounts and paints the widget. KkPhaseBuilder seeds its phase from kkFrameTime() when it starts (line 52), KkLoop does not. So a running KkHazard, KkMarquee or KkCrt that appears while the app is running paints one frame at loop time 0 and jumps to the shared clock on the next frame: the stripes jump by up to a tile, the ticker text jumps by up to a unit, the sweep line shows at the top edge for one frame. That contradicts the stated rule that all loops share the frame clock and stay in step, and it is a visible single-frame hitch exactly when an alarm band appears.
evidence:
Throwaway test: harness pumped with motion on for 1325ms, then a Column with `KkHazard(width: 200, height: 24, running: true)`, `KkMarquee('ALERT', period: 1s, gap: 20)` and `KkCrt(sweep: true, ...)` mounted with a single `tester.pumpWidget`, and the painters sampled with a recording canvas on that frame and the next two (16ms apart):

  first frame : frameTime=1325ms hazard right=237.59 marquee x0=0.00 sweep y=0.00  (shared clock says hazard right=253.62)
  second frame: frameTime=1341ms hazard right=254.22 marquee x0=-21.89 sweep y=26.82  (shared clock says hazard right=254.22)
  third frame : frameTime=1357ms hazard right=254.82 marquee x0=-22.92 sweep y=27.14  (shared clock says hazard right=254.82)
  Expected: 253.61555370689507 (±0.05)
    Actual: <237.58787536621094>
  the first frame is already in step
suggestedFix: Seed the clock when the loop starts, before the first paint, as KkPhaseBuilder does: in `_sync()`, in the `shouldRun` branch, set `_time.value` to the scaled `kkFrameTime()` (the same expression `_tick` uses) before or after starting the ticker.

title: Changing KeikaiApp.glitchOnAlert replays the screen glitch and the three red flashes
explanation: Found while tracing what feeds KkGlitch.trigger (KkGlitch itself fires correctly, only on a trigger change). KeikaiApp passes `trigger: widget.glitchOnAlert ? _alerts : 0`. Once the app has turned to alert at least once, `_alerts` is 1 or more, so flipping the option changes the trigger value (n -> 0 or 0 -> n) although the condition did not change, and KkGlitch plays the full glitch with the red flashes. In particular, switching the effect off (for example from a 'reduce flashing' setting bound to `glitchOnAlert`) makes the whole screen glitch and flash red three times at that moment.
evidence:
Throwaway test with `Widget app(KkCondition c, {bool glitch = true}) => KeikaiApp(condition: c, glitchOnAlert: glitch, home: const SizedBox(width: 10, height: 10));`: standby, then alert (glitch plays and finishes), then the same alert app with glitchOnAlert false, wait, then true again; RenderKkGlitch.progress read right after each pumpWidget:

  alert entered: progress=0.0
  glitch done:   progress=1.0
  glitchOnAlert true -> false: progress=0.0 flash=Color(alpha: 1.0000, red: 0.9725, green: 0.1569, blue: 0.2353, colorSpace: ColorSpace.sRGB)
  glitchOnAlert false -> true: progress=0.0
  Expected: [1.0, 1.0]
    Actual: [0.0, 0.0]
  no glitch without a turn to alert
suggestedFix: Do not fold the option into the trigger value. Pass `trigger: _alerts` and gate the count instead: increment `_alerts` in `_setCondition` and `didUpdateWidget` only when `widget.glitchOnAlert` is true (or give KkGlitch an `enabled` flag that is checked when the trigger changes).

title: Dashed KkEdges sides are not fitted to the side: the run starts at the left/top of each band and is cut off where the side ends, so small boxes come out lopsided
explanation: KkEdges.paint (lines 255-265) uses dash = max(3, 3*width), gap = dash, and simply steps from band.left / band.top. The left and right bands start below the top band (lines 270-271), so their first dash always hangs under the top corners and whatever does not fit at the far end is dropped. A side shorter than one period plus a dash gets exactly one dash, at its start. The top-left corner is therefore always solid while the right and bottom corners depend on size modulo the period, and vertical sides are top-heavy. The package's own 'skipped' step mark hits this in normal use: lib/src/hud/sequence.dart builds a 16x16 box (_markSize, line 206) with KkEdges.line(edge, width: m.stroke2, dashed: true) (line 334) for bundle.css line 1797 (.kk-seq__mark { border-style: dashed } on a 16px box with a 2px border). It is drawn with vertical dashes only in its upper half and two stubs at the bottom, not as a dashed square. Browsers fit the dashes so every side begins and ends with a dash (CSS Backgrounds 3 asks implementations to choose a spacing that makes the corners symmetrical). The same code also leaves the top-right / bottom-right corner pixel open on 1px dashed panels, chips, fields and the empty state whenever (width - 1) mod 6 >= 3.
evidence:
Throwaway test: KkEdges.line(white, width: 2, dashed: true).paint(canvas, Rect.fromLTWH(0, 0, 16, 16)), rendered to a 16x16 image and checked for mirror symmetry (expect(asymmetric, 0)).
Output:
16x16, 2.0px dashed:
######......####
######......####
##............##
##............##
##............##
##............##
##............##
##............##
................
................
................
................
................
................
######......####
######......####
corner pixels TL=true TR=true BL=true BR=true; pixels without a mirror twin: 64
Expected: <0>
  Actual: <64>
suggestedFix: Fit the run to each side. For a side of length L: n = max(1, ((L + gap) / (dash + gap)).round()) dashes, fitted gap g = n > 1 ? (L - n * dash) / (n - 1) : 0, dash i at start + i * (dash + g); paint the side solid when L <= 2 * dash. Run the left and right sides over the full height (r.top..r.bottom) so both ends share a corner dash with the top and bottom sides, and collect all dashes in one Path so a translucent colour is not blended twice at the corners.

title: Borders and line patterns are painted on whatever fractional rectangle layout produces; 1px lines smear over two pixels in KkGrid cells and text-sized boxes
explanation: KkEdges.paint (lines 245-272), kkPaintSurface, the bracket painter and every pattern painter in patterns.dart (scan lines 184-186, ticks 229-231, grid 248-253, segments 262-265) take the rect as given and draw anti-aliased axis-aligned rectangles on it. Nothing between layout and the canvas rounds to the pixel grid, and the package's own layout hands them non-integer rects in normal use: RenderKkGrid places cells at column * (colWidth + gutter) with colWidth = (width - gutters) / cols (lib/src/layout/grid.dart lines 324-336), and a box that hugs text gets the font's fractional advance width. The result is that stroke-1 lines are no longer 1px: they become two columns at partial alpha, with a different split for every panel, and the 1-on / 2-off scan-line structure turns into 2 half-strength rows. In the CSS source of truth, border and background rectangles are snapped to device pixels at paint time, so these lines are always one crisp pixel. For a language built on 1px hairlines this is visible at most window widths (any width where (W - gutters) is not divisible by the column count) and on the right edge of most tags, chips and buttons.
evidence:
Throwaway tests (pixel ratio 1, alpha read back from a RepaintBoundary / Picture):
1) KkGrid(stagger: false, children: 4 x KkCell(span: 3, rows: 1, child: KkBox(edges: KkEdges.line(white)))) pumped at Size(1365, 100):
grid width 1280.0: cell 1 left=322.00 -> alpha[322]=255 alpha[323]=0; ... (crisp)
grid width 1365.0: cell 1 left=343.25 -> alpha[343]=192 alpha[344]=64; cell 2 left=686.50 -> alpha[686]=128 alpha[687]=128; cell 3 left=1029.75 -> alpha[1029]=64 alpha[1030]=192
Expected: true  Actual: <false>
2) KkBox(height: 24, padding: horizontal 8, alignment: center, shrinkWrap: true, edges: KkEdges.line(white), child: Text('COOLANT TEMP', Sofia Sans Extra Condensed 13/700)) with the bundled fonts loaded:
tag rect Rect.fromLTRB(0.0, 0.0, 77.8, 24.0); alpha of the 1px right border at x=75..78: [0, 51, 205, 0]
3) const KkScanPattern(color: black).paint(canvas, Rect.fromLTWH(0, 0.5, 10, 12)):
alpha down one column: [0, 0, 128, 128, 0, 128, 128, 0, 128, 128, 0, 128, 128, 0]  (expected four rows at 255)
suggestedFix: Snap before painting. Simplest at the source: in RenderKkGrid round each track edge (x0 = (column * (colWidth + gutter)).roundToDouble(), width = rounded right edge - x0) and let a shrink-wrapped RenderKkBox ceil a text-derived size to whole pixels, so the painters keep receiving integer rects. Alternatively round the rect to whole physical pixels at the top of KkDecoration.paintBackground / paintForeground and kkPaintSurface (left/top/right/bottom each rounded, not width/height) so borders, brackets and patterns share one snapped rectangle.

title: kkDashPath: phase is reduced modulo the pattern sum, which is wrong for odd-length patterns (their period is twice the sum)
explanation: The loop handles an odd-length pattern the SVG way (the on/off roles swap on every pass, so [5] means 5 on / 5 off and [5,3,2] means 5,3,2,5,3,2), but line 336 computes `distance = -(phase % total)` with total = sum of the list. For an odd-length list the real period is 2 * total, so any phase in [total, 2*total), and every negative phase, lands on the wrong half of the cycle and the dashes come out inverted. A marching-dash animation that advances phase past the sum (or counts down, as the CSS kk-flow keyframes do with stroke-dashoffset: -16) flips on/off once per cycle. Even-length patterns are fine, and no caller in the package passes phase today, so this is latent in the exported API.
evidence:
Throwaway test on the line (0,0)->(20,0), printing the x-range of each dash:
expect(runs(kkDashPath(line, const <double>[5, 5], phase: 5)), ['5.0..10.0', '15.0..20.0']);  // passes
expect(runs(kkDashPath(line, const <double>[5], phase: 5)), ['5.0..10.0', '15.0..20.0']);
  Expected: ['5.0..10.0', '15.0..20.0']
    Actual: ['0.0..5.0', '10.0..15.0']
expect(runs(kkDashPath(line, const <double>[5, 3, 2], phase: 10)), ['5.0..8.0', '10.0..15.0', '18.0..20.0']);  // same as [5,3,2,5,3,2] with phase 10
  Expected: ['5.0..8.0', '10.0..15.0', '18.0..20.0']
    Actual: ['0.0..5.0', '8.0..10.0', '15.0..18.0']
suggestedFix: Use the true period: `final double period = pattern.length.isOdd ? total * 2 : total; double distance = -(phase % period);`. The rest of the loop already alternates correctly.

title: kkParseSvgPath accepts path data that does not begin with a moveto and draws it from (0,0) instead of throwing
explanation: The SVG grammar requires path data to start with M or m; anything else is an error and a browser renders nothing. The parser only checks that the first token is some command letter (lines 95-99), so 'L10 10', 'H5', 'A...', 'l5 5 z' and a bare 'Z' are accepted and Flutter's Path silently starts them at the origin. The doc comment promises a FormatException for data that is not valid path data, and the existing 'bad data throws' test covers '10 10' but not this case. A custom KkIconData whose stroke lost its leading M therefore paints a stray line from the icon's top-left corner instead of failing loudly. (For valid input the parser is sound: a differential fuzz of 4000 random paths with packed numbers, packed arc flags, implicit repeats and every command against an independent reference showed 0 mismatches.)
evidence:
Throwaway test:
for (final String bad in ['L10 10', 'H5', 'Z', 'l5 5z', 'A5 5 0 0 1 10 0']) expect(() => kkParseSvgPath(bad), throwsFormatException, reason: '"$bad"');
  Expected: throws <Instance of 'FormatException'>
    Actual: <Closure: () => Path>
     Which: returned _NativePath:<Path>
  "L10 10"
Probe output: OK "L10 10" -> [len=14.142 closed=false start=(0.000,0.000) end=(10.000,10.000)]; OK "H5" -> [len=5.000 ... start=(0.000,0.000) end=(5.000,0.000)]; OK "l5 5 z" -> [len=14.142 closed=true ...]
suggestedFix: Track whether a moveto has been seen: when the first command read is not 0x4D / 0x6D, throw FormatException('Path data must begin with a moveto', src, _i - 1).

title: kkPaintGlow blurs the shape inflated by the ring, so the halo sits `ring` px further out than the box-shadow it implements
explanation: The glow tokens are two independent shadows of the border box: `0 0 0 1px c` (the ring, spread 1) and `0 0 18px c@0.3` (the halo, spread 0). Line 174 builds the halo from shape.path(rect.inflate(glow.ring)), i.e. it gives the halo the ring's 1px spread as well, so at every distance d from the box the painted halo has the intensity CSS has at d - 1. The blur sigma (blur / 2), the outside-only painting and the ring itself are correct. The error is small (up to 4/255 of alpha next to the ring for glow-signal) but it is a systematic 1px enlargement of every glow.
evidence:
Throwaway test: box edge at x = 100, KkGlow(color: red, ring: 1, blur: 18, alpha: 0.3) against the same glow with ring: 0 (which is exactly what `0 0 18px` paints), alpha of one pixel row:
x=84..98 ring=1: [3, 5, 6, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 18, 20, 23, 27, 30, 33, 37]
x=84..98 ring=0: [3, 3, 5, 6, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 18, 20, 23, 27, 30, 33]
Expected: [3, 3, 5, 6, ...]  Actual: [3, 5, 6, 7, ...]  Which: at location [1] is <5> instead of <3>
(the ring=1 profile is the ring=0 profile shifted one pixel outward)
suggestedFix: Blur the un-inflated outline: `canvas.drawPath(shape.path(rect), haloPaint)`. With BlurStyle.outer the halo then starts at the box edge and the ring, which is painted afterwards, covers its first `ring` pixels exactly as in CSS.

title: KkBracketSpec clamps both arms by half of the shorter side, so a box under 24px tall gets shortened horizontal arms
explanation: Line 301: `l = min(length, min(r.width, r.height) / 2)` and the same l is used for horizontal and vertical arms. bundle.css lines 113-122 give every horizontal arm a fixed 12x2 background tile and every vertical arm 2x12; an arm is only cut by the box along its own axis. On a wide box that is less than 24px tall (after the outset) the vertical arms of the two corners meet, which is the same picture in both, but the Dart horizontal arms shrink to height / 2 while the CSS ones stay 12px. KkBrackets around a small tag, key cap or one-line readout is the case that shows it.
evidence:
Throwaway test: const KkBracketSpec(color: red).paint(canvas, const Rect.fromLTWH(4, 4, 100, 14)) (a 100x14 element, so the bracket box is 102x16), counting opaque pixels of the top-left horizontal arm:
top-left horizontal arm length: 8
Expected: <12>
  Actual: <8>
suggestedFix: Clamp per axis: `final double lx = math.min(length, r.width / 2); final double ly = math.min(length, r.height / 2);` and use lx for the four horizontal rects and ly for the four vertical ones.

title: KkEdges.paint paints outside the rect when a side is wider than the rect
explanation: The bands are built from the raw widths (lines 268-271): top is r.top..r.top + top.width, bottom is r.bottom - bottom.width..r.bottom, and left/right run from r.top + top.width to r.bottom - bottom.width. When the box has been squeezed below its own border widths (RenderKkBox can be constrained smaller than its insets; CSS border-box sizing cannot), the top and bottom bands spill past the opposite edge and the left/right bands get top > bottom. A 2px-high box with a stroke-4 top edge paints two extra rows below itself; with a translucent colour overlapping bands are also blended twice.
evidence:
Throwaway test: const KkEdges(top: KkSide(red, width: 4)).paint(canvas, const Rect.fromLTWH(2, 6, 40, 2)), counting painted pixels whose centre is outside the rect:
pixels painted outside Rect.fromLTRB(2.0, 6.0, 42.0, 8.0): 80
Expected: <0>
  Actual: <80>
suggestedFix: Clamp the widths to the rect before building the bands, e.g. `final double t = math.min(top.width, r.height); final double b = math.min(bottom.width, r.height - t);` (and the same for left/right against r.width), and skip a band whose extent is not positive.

title: kkPaintIcon leaves the canvas saved, translated and scaled when the path data fails to parse, displacing everything painted after the icon
explanation: kkPaintIcon calls canvas.save(), translate and scale (lines 17-19) and only then parses the path strings lazily through the caches (lines 21, 32, 35). kkParseSvgPath throws FormatException for malformed data, so the function exits without canvas.restore(). RenderObject catches the paint exception and carries on painting the rest of the layer with the icon's transform still applied, so one mistyped custom KkIconData does not just lose that icon: every sibling painted after it in the same picture is moved and scaled, on every frame, in release builds too.
evidence:
Throwaway widget test: Stack[Positioned(left: 20, top: 10, child: KkIcon(KkIconData('bad', stroke: 'M0 0 L5'), size: 32)), Positioned(left: 60, top: 10, child: KkBox(width: 10, height: 10, fill: red))] inside a RepaintBoundary, then the bounding box of the painted red pixels:
paint exception: FormatException: Expected a number (at character 8)
red box laid out at Rect.fromLTRB(60.0, 10.0, 70.0, 20.0); painted at x 140..159, y 30..49
Expected: [60, 69, 10, 19]
  Actual: [140, 159, 30, 49]
And on a bare canvas: save count before=1 after=2, translation left on canvas: (10.0, 10.0)
suggestedFix: Resolve the three paths (fill, stroke, dashed) through the caches before canvas.save(), or wrap the body in try { ... } finally { canvas.restore(); } so a FormatException cannot leak canvas state.

title: The dashed plate of status-offline is stroked with butt caps; the data URI gives every dash a square cap
explanation: The path data of all five status glyphs matches bundle.css lines 29-33 exactly, and stroke width, joins, miter limit, the even-odd critical plate and the 1.8 squares are right. The one difference is line 36: `line..strokeCap = StrokeCap.butt` for the dashed path. In the data URI on line 32 stroke-linecap='square' is set on the <svg> root and is inherited by the path that carries stroke-dasharray='2.6 1.9', and SVG caps every dash, so each dash is 2.6 + 2 * 0.75 = 4.1 long with 0.4 gaps. Flutter draws 2.6 on / 1.9 off, so the offline glyph has visibly more open dashes than the web one (about 30 percent less ink at 12px). Whether to follow the CSS literally is a design call, since the README wants the offline plate to read as dashed and the web gaps are only 0.3px at 12px, but as written the Flutter glyph is not the glyph the data URI describes.
evidence:
bundle.css line 32: <svg ... stroke-width='1.5' stroke-linecap='square'><path d='M5 1.75H14.25V14.25H1.75V5Z' stroke-dasharray='2.6 1.9'/><path d='M4.9 8h6.2'/></svg>
Throwaway test comparing kkPaintIcon(statusOffline) with the same two paths drawn with StrokeCap.square on every dash (dashes cut by hand with PathMetric.extractPath):
size 12: ink dart=30.4px svg=43.6px, pixels differing by >96/255: 14
size 48: ink dart=492.6px svg=696.9px, pixels differing by >96/255: 235
suggestedFix: To match the source, keep the square cap for the dashed path (drop `..strokeCap = StrokeCap.butt`). If the more open dashes are preferred for legibility, keep butt caps but say so in the KkIconData / kkStatusIcon documentation as a deliberate deviation from the data URI.

title: Dialog corner brackets sit 1px too far out: CSS inset -6px is measured from the padding box, KkBracketSpec.outset from the border box
explanation: Outside the seven assigned files; found while checking how KkBracketSpec.outset is consumed. KkBracketSpec.paint inflates the rect it is given, and RenderKkBox passes its full size, i.e. the border box (edges take space inside the box). In CSS the bracket pseudo-element is absolutely positioned, so its inset is measured from the padding edge of the positioned parent. bundle.css line 1433 has .kk-dialog::before { inset: -6px } on a dialog with a 1px border (line 1427), which is 5px outside the border box. dialog.dart line 180 passes outset: 6. The panel already applies this conversion: .kk-panel::before has inset -1px (line 110) and lib/src/hud/panel.dart line 240 correctly uses outset: 0.
evidence:
bundle.css 1420-1433: `.kk-dialog { position: relative; ... border: var(--stroke-1) solid var(--signal); }` and `.kk-dialog::before { position: absolute; inset: -6px; ... }` -> bracket box = padding box + 6 = border box + 5.
dialog.dart line 180: `brackets: KkBracketSpec(color: frame, length: m.space3, width: m.stroke2, outset: 6),` on a KkBox whose decoration has `edges: KkEdges.line(frame, width: m.stroke1)` -> bracket box = border box + 6. Concrete input: any KkDialog; each bracket is 1px further from the frame than in CSS (the bracket rectangle is 2px wider and taller).
suggestedFix: Use `outset: 6 - m.stroke1` (5).

title: Field focus brackets sit 1px too far out for the same reason (CSS inset -5px from the padding box, outset 5 from the border box)
explanation: Outside the seven assigned files; same cause as the dialog finding. bundle.css line 1018 has .kk-field__box::before { inset: -5px } and .kk-field__box has position: relative and a 1px border (lines 1005-1013), so the brackets are 4px outside the border box. field.dart passes outset: 5 to a KkBox whose border box is the same box (the focus state only thickens the border inwards).
evidence:
bundle.css 1005-1018: `.kk-field__box { position: relative; ... border: var(--stroke-1) solid var(--ink-faint); }`, `.kk-field__box::before { position: absolute; inset: -5px; ... }` -> border box + 4.
field.dart line 140: `? KkBracketSpec(color: accent, length: m.space2, width: m.stroke2, outset: 5)` next to `edges: KkEdges.line(edge, width: m.stroke1 + ring, dashed: !enabled)` -> border box + 5. Concrete input: any focused field with brackets.
suggestedFix: Use `outset: 5 - m.stroke1` (4).

title: glowTrace (and the level-coloured trace glow) is half as wide as the CSS drop-shadow it copies
explanation: Outside the seven assigned files; found while checking KkGlow against shadow semantics. KkGlow.blur is defined as a box-shadow blur radius whose Gaussian sigma is half of it, and both kkPaintGlow and the trace painter use blur / 2 as sigma. The glow-trace token (0 0 4px #5cff9d99) is consumed by filter: drop-shadow() (bundle.css line 508), and in drop-shadow the length is the standard deviation itself, not a blur radius. The rest of the package already converts this way: drop-shadow(0 0 6px) becomes blur: 12 in button.dart line 136 and icon_button.dart line 132, and drop-shadow(0 0 8px) becomes blur: 16 in fab.dart line 120 (with a comment saying so). glowTrace keeps blur: 4, so the trace bloom is drawn with sigma 2 instead of 4; the level-coloured variant in charts/trace.dart line 95 uses blur: 3 for drop-shadow(0 0 3px currentColor) (bundle.css line 510), sigma 1.5 instead of 3.
evidence:
colors.dart line 198: `KkGlow get glowTrace => KkGlow(color: nominal, ring: 0, blur: 4, alpha: 0.6);`
charts/trace.dart line 95: `... : KkGlow(color: ink, ring: 0, blur: 3, alpha: 1);` and line 236: `..maskFilter = MaskFilter.blur(BlurStyle.normal, g.blur / 2)` -> sigma 2 and 1.5.
bundle.css 508 / 510: `filter: drop-shadow(var(--glow-trace));` with --glow-trace 0 0 4px, and `filter: drop-shadow(0 0 3px currentColor);` -> sigma 4 and 3.
Same package, same conversion done right: fab.dart line 120 `KkGlow(color: fill, ring: 0, blur: 16, alpha: 1)` for drop-shadow(0 0 8px).
suggestedFix: Set glowTrace to `blur: 8` and the fallback in trace.dart to `blur: 6`, matching the convention used by the button, icon button and FAB glows.

title: Meter bar (and the controlled timer's bar) never moves while its value changes more often than every 50ms
explanation: Every change of `value` is handed to `KkSteppedValue`, which sets `_from = _current()` and restarts its 0.45s / 9-step run from zero (lib/src/motion/entrances.dart:340-346 and 319-327). `steps(9, end)` holds the old value for the first 50ms of a run, so when the next change arrives sooner than that the run is restarted before its first step, again and again. The lit bar stays at the value it had when the updates began for as long as they keep coming, while the number beside it is correct. Any source faster than 20Hz does this: an AnimatedBuilder, a ticker-driven simulation, 30Hz telemetry. `KkTimer(value:, progress:)` has the same problem (lib/src/hud/timer.dart:395-401): a controlled timer has to be rebuilt every frame to show centiseconds, and a progress computed from the same time leaves the bar frozen at its first value. The self-running countdown only avoids it by quantising its bar to whole seconds (timer.dart:320-322), which makes that bar up to one second late: a 3s countdown still shows 33% when it reaches zero and 100% for its whole first second.
evidence:
Throwaway widget tests, motion on; `bar` is the `value` field of the bar's CustomPainter.

Meter: `KkBox(width: 320, child: KkMeter(value: value, unit: '%'))`, value raised linearly 0 -> 0.9 over 3s, one setState + `tester.pump(16ms)` per step:
M1[16] t=592ms value=0.178 bar=0.000
M1[16] t=1184ms value=0.356 bar=0.000
M1[16] t=1776ms value=0.534 bar=0.000
M1[16] t=2368ms value=0.712 bar=0.000
M1[16] t=2960ms value=0.890 bar=0.000
M1[16] texts: 090 %
Expected: a numeric value within <0.11> of <0.9>
  Actual: <0.0>
Same result (bar=0.000 throughout) at 33ms and at 40ms per update; at 50ms the bar moves (0.765 at the end).

Controlled timer: `KkTimer(value: ..., progress: progress, boot: false)`, progress lowered 1 -> 0.5 with `tester.pump(16ms)` per step:
P2 t=960ms progress=0.900 bar=1.0
P2 t=2880ms progress=0.700 bar=1.0
P2 t=4800ms progress=0.500 bar=1.0
Expected: a numeric value within <0.06> of <0.5>
  Actual: <1.0>

Countdown workaround, `KkTimer.countdown(from: Duration(seconds: 3))` sampled every 100ms: bar=1.000 until `t=1000 digits=00:02.00`, and `P8 t=3000 digits=00:00.00 bar=0.333`.
suggestedFix: Fix the retargeting in `_KkSteppedValueState.didUpdateWidget` (lib/src/motion/entrances.dart:340-346): when a run is still in flight keep its clock and change only the target, re-basing `_from` so the value shown now does not jump (with s the stepped progress and `shown = _current()`: `_to = widget.value; _from = (shown - _to * s) / (1 - s)`), and start a fresh run only when the previous one has finished. Every run then reaches the latest target within 0.45s however often the value changes. With that in place the countdown can pass its real `left / from` instead of whole seconds (timer.dart:320-322).

title: Head rows carry 8px more than the CSS: the status word is clipped at the documented 208px minimum
explanation: The CSS head is a flex row with `gap: 8px` and three items, the last one pushed right by `margin-left: auto` (bundle.css 354-358, 401-405, 454-457), so its minimum width is cjk + 8 + en + 8 + right item. The widgets put a `KkSpacer()` between the labels and the right-hand item inside a row with `gap: m.space2`. The spacer is a fourth flex child, so the row gap is applied on both of its sides and the minimum becomes cjk + 8 + en + 8 + 0 + 8 + right item, 8px more than the design. Two consequences. (1) A readout held at its documented 208px minimum clips the status word of the README sample (the row clips with Clip.hardEdge), although the CSS layout fits with 3.9px to spare; the status word is one of the three signals a level must always show. (2) Hugging instruments whose head is their widest row are up to 8px wider than the web ones (the sample readout hugs to 212.1 instead of 208). The meter head (lib/src/hud/meter.dart:144-152) and the timer head (lib/src/hud/timer.dart:370-378) are built the same way.
evidence:
`KkBox(width: 208, child: KkReadout(cjk: '冷却水温', en: 'coolant temp', value: '042.7', unit: '°C', level: KkLevel.nominal, scramble: false, boot: false))`, content box 208 - 24 = 184:
H1 NOMINAL: box=208.0 content=184 cjk=44.80 en=67.73 state=51.57 cssNeeded=180.10 stateLeft=136.53 wordRight=216.10 contentRight=212.0 cutOff=4.10px
H1 CRITICAL: box=208.0 content=184 cjk=44.80 en=66.56 state=52.57 cssNeeded=179.93 stateLeft=135.36 wordRight=215.93 contentRight=212.0 cutOff=3.93px
Expected: a value less than or equal to <212.5>
  Actual: <216.09641647338867>
A 3x capture of that test showed the words as 'NOMINA' and 'CRITICA'.

Hug widths with long labels against the CSS sum (cjk + 8 + en + 8 + right item, plus padding and border):
R2 readout: css=266.22 flutter=274.22
R2 meter: css=270.14 flutter=278.14
R2 timer: css=376.67 flutter=384.67
(each exactly 8px wider)

The same head rebuilt as two children pushed apart (below) measured `word.right=184.00 overflow=0.00` in a 184px row, with unchanged vertical positions of the three parts.
suggestedFix: Do not put the spacer between gaps. Build the head as two children pushed apart: `KkRow(gap: m.space2, main: KkMainAlign.between, cross: KkCrossAlign.baseline, clip: Clip.hardEdge, children: [KkRow(shrinkWrap: true, gap: m.space2, cross: KkCrossAlign.baseline, children: [cjk, en]), rightItem])`, keeping `KkAlignSelf(center)` on the readout's status word. Apply the same change to the meter head (meter.dart:144-175) and the timer head (timer.dart:370-381).

title: A self-running timer on a covered page does not pause, reports done late and gives its controller stale state
explanation: The countdown and the stopwatch take their time from the Ticker's elapsed value (`_run = elapsed`) and do everything else inside the tick: repaint, `onDone`, and what the controller reports. When tickers are muted (TickerMode off, which is what happens to every page under an opaque `KkPageRoute`) no tick is delivered, but the ticker's elapsed time keeps running from its original start. So the timer does not pause, contrary to its own doc (lines 86-87: 'they pause while their route is off screen'): when the page comes back the whole covered time is added at once. While the page is covered a countdown that runs out does not call `onDone` until the page is uncovered, `controller.isRunning` stays true and `controller.elapsed` stays at the last painted value. An alarm countdown on a page the operator has navigated away from therefore fires late by however long the other page stays open.
evidence:
`KeikaiApp(home: KkTimer.countdown(from: Duration(seconds: 5), controller: controller, onDone: ...))`; at t=1s `navigator.push(KkPageRoute(...))`, wait 10.5s, then pop:
N1 t=1s digits=00:04.00 elapsed=0:00:01.000000
N1 covered for 10.5s (countdown should have ended at t=5s): done=0 isRunning=true elapsed=0:00:01.000000 digits=00:04.00
N1 back on top: done=1 doneAt=0:00:11.500000 isRunning=false digits=00:00.00
Expected: <1>
  Actual: <0>

Same with `KkTimer.stopwatch`, covered at 2s for 30s:
N2 t=2s digits=00:02.00
N2 covered 30s: elapsed=0:00:02.000000 isRunning=true
N2 back on top after 16ms: digits=00:32.01 elapsed=0:00:32.016000

The same with a plain `TickerMode(enabled: false)` around a stopwatch for 5s: expected '00:01.10' (paused), actual '00:06.10'.
suggestedFix: Decide which behaviour is meant and implement it in the state instead of leaving it to the ticker. To pause as documented: read `TickerMode.of(context)` in `didChangeDependencies`; when it turns off while running, bank `_run`, stop the ticker and remember that the timer is suspended; start the ticker again when it turns back on. To keep wall-clock time instead: measure elapsed time independently of frames and arm a `Timer` for the time left, so `onDone`, `elapsed` and `isRunning` do not depend on ticks, and correct the doc comment.

title: KkTimerController listeners are not told about autostart, restart or removal of the timer
explanation: `KkTimerController` promises that listeners are told when the timer starts, stops, is reset or runs out (lines 50-51), and `isRunning` is what a start/stop control reads. Three state changes are silent: the autostart in `initState` (`_start(notify: false)`, line 227; `autostart` defaults to true), the restart in `didUpdateWidget` when `from` or the kind changes (line 241), and the detach in `dispose` (line 247), which turns `isRunning` false. A listener that was built before the timer in the same frame (a toolbar above the timer) shows 'stopped' for a running timer until some other event rebuilds it, and its first press then does the opposite of its label.
evidence:
`KkColumn(children: [ListenableBuilder(listenable: controller, builder: (_, _) => KkText.en(controller.isRunning ? 'running' : 'stopped')), KkTimer.stopwatch(controller: controller)])`, then `tester.pump(1s)`:
P4 isRunning=true notified=0 digits=00:01.00
P4 label shows: STOPPED
Expected: exactly one matching candidate
  Actual: _TextWidgetFinder:<Found 0 widgets with text "RUNNING": []>

A finished 1s countdown rebuilt with `from: Duration(seconds: 5)`:
P4b finished: running=false notified=1
P4b restarted: running=true notified=1 digits=00:04.50
Expected: a value greater than <1>
  Actual: <1>

A running stopwatch removed from the tree:
E2 timer removed: isRunning=false notified=0
suggestedFix: After attaching and auto-starting (initState), after the restart in didUpdateWidget and after detaching in dispose, notify the controller once outside the build, for example `SchedulerBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback((_) => controller._changed())` on the controller captured at that moment (skip it if the controller has been disposed), instead of suppressing the notification.

title: With an action the alert bar's live region reads the alarm twice
explanation: The bar gives its semantics node a label made of title, sub and code and normally hides its own text with `ExcludeSemantics`. When an `action` is given, `excluding` is false for the whole subtree, so the visible texts (cjk, title, sub, code) are merged into the same live-region node after the label. A screen reader announces every alarm that has an acknowledge button twice, the second time in capitals and with the CJK word. The action itself is fine: it keeps its own button node, is focusable, and tap and Enter both reach `onPressed`.
evidence:
`tester.ensureSemantics()`; critical bar with cjk '警報', title 'critical — coolant pressure low', sub '冷却水圧 低下 · SEC-04', code 'E-4127'.
Without action:
A1 #4 label=critical — coolant pressure low, 冷却水圧 低下 · SEC-04, E-4127 value= flags=[isLiveRegion] actions=0
With `action: KkPressable(onPressed: () {}, builder: (_, _) => const KkText.en('ack'))`:
A1 #4 label=critical — coolant pressure low, 冷却水圧 低下 · SEC-04, E-4127 ⏎ 警報 ⏎ CRITICAL — COOLANT PRESSURE LOW ⏎ 冷却水圧 低下 · SEC-04 ⏎ E-4127 value= flags=[isLiveRegion] actions=0
A1   #5 label=ACK value= flags=[isButton, hasEnabledState, isEnabled, isFocusable] actions=4194305
A1 title occurs 2 time(s) in the bar label
Expected: <1>
  Actual: <2>
suggestedFix: Exclude the text parts unconditionally and leave only the action in the semantics tree: wrap the hazards, the main block and the code block in `ExcludeSemantics` (each, or as one group that does not contain `trailing`) instead of switching the exclusion off for the whole row when there is an action.

title: kkFormatTimer prints a signed zero, -00:00:00, in the hours format
explanation: The sign is dropped only when the time is shorter than one centisecond (`totalCs > 0`), whatever the format. In `HH:MM:SS` the smallest unit shown is a second, so every time between -1s and -10ms prints `-00:00:00`. The same function avoids exactly this for the centisecond format (-4ms prints `00:00.00`, and the existing test names the rule: 'a rounding-size negative has none'). A controlled timer in `KkTimerFormat.hours` that crosses zero shows `-00:00:00` for a second.
evidence:
`kkFormatTimer(const Duration(milliseconds: -500), format: KkTimerFormat.hours)`:
P1 hours(-500ms) -> -00:00:00
P1 hours(-4ms) -> 00:00:00
P1 auto(-4ms) -> 00:00.00
Expected: '00:00:00'
  Actual: '-00:00:00'
suggestedFix: Work out `hours` before the sign and test the smallest unit that is displayed: `final bool nonZero = hours ? totalSeconds > 0 : totalCs > 0; final String sign = (time.isNegative && nonZero) ? '-' : '';`.

title: A countdown that starts with nothing left never calls onDone
explanation: `_start` returns before doing anything when a countdown has no time left, and `onDone` is only called from `_onTick`. A countdown whose `from` is zero or negative (a deadline that has already passed when the widget is built, `from: deadline.difference(now)`) is at zero from its first frame but never reports done, although the constructor says it 'counts down from [from] to zero and then calls [onDone]'. Code that waits for `onDone` waits forever.
evidence:
`KkTimer.countdown(from: Duration.zero, onDone: () => done++)`, then two `tester.pump(1s)`:
P5 zero countdown: done=0 digits=00:00.00
Expected: <1>
  Actual: <0>
suggestedFix: When a countdown is started (autostart or `controller.start()`) with nothing left and `_doneFired` is still false, set `_doneFired` and call `onDone` (after the frame when this happens in initState or didUpdateWidget), then notify the controller.

title: Empty strings are laid out as content: phantom gaps, lines and head rows
explanation: The optional parts are tested with `!= null` only, so an empty string keeps its slot with its gap, padding or line. Alert bar: `cjk: ''` indents the title by 16px (line 105), `sub: ''` adds an empty 12px line so the bar is 67px instead of 64 and the title sits 9px higher (line 119), `code: ''` reserves 32px (line 134). Timer: `cjk`, `en` or `mode` of `''` adds an empty 30px head row (lib/src/hud/timer.dart:369). Readout: `cjk: ''` indents the label by 8px (lib/src/hud/readout.dart:132), and a readout with no label and no status word still builds its head row, so the value starts 22px from the top instead of 14 (readout.dart:127; the timer omits its head in the same situation). `KkLabel` in lib/src/widgets/text.dart already treats an empty string as absent.
evidence:
E1 alert: absent -> title=Rect.fromLTRB(82.0, 19.0, 518.0, 45.0) bar=Size(600.0, 64.0)
E1 alert: empty  -> title=Rect.fromLTRB(98.0, 10.0, 486.0, 36.0) bar=Size(600.0, 67.0)
E1 timer: absent -> Size(264.0, 94.0)   empty -> Size(264.0, 124.0)
E1 readout: en label x with cjk absent=12.0, with cjk empty=20.0
E1 readout without any head content: value starts 22.0px from the top (border 2 + padding 12 = 14), box=Size(208.0, 66.0)
Expected: <82.0>
  Actual: <98.0>
(`KkAlertBar(title: 'advisory')` against `KkAlertBar(cjk: '', title: 'advisory', sub: '', code: '')` in a 600px box; `KkTimer(value: 3s)` against the same with `cjk: '', en: '', mode: ''`; `KkReadout(en: 'pressure', value: '094.1')` against the same with `cjk: ''`; `KkReadout(value: '094.1')`.)
suggestedFix: Normalise the optional strings once at the top of each build (`final String? big = (cjk == null || cjk!.isEmpty) ? null : cjk;` and the same for sub, code, en, unit, mode, state) in the alert bar, readout, meter and timer, and build the readout's head row only when it has a label or a status word.
